title: A closing agent cannot remove the closed sprint's runner worktree and branches, because git worktree remove and git branch -D are denied to agents, so every autopilot sprint leaves them behind
goal: backlog.py close (a python process, like land, which already removes worker worktrees and the landed branch) removes the closed sprint's runner leftovers itself: the runner-SP-* worktree under the clone root, the orch/SP branch, the clean detached or work/<id> agent-* worktrees of that sprint, empty worktree-agent-* branches whose tip is on the integration main, and _cache/autopilot/SP; never --force, never another sprint's, never a locked, dirty or process-holding worktree (kept and reported with the reason); the skill step then only reports. Planted tests (name close_removes_runner_leftovers): a throwaway clone with each leftover removed, another sprint's kept, a dirty one kept. Found by the first supervised run (BG-s2ejyxwb) and mac-third's landing: agents are denied the commands, so leftovers accumulate across unattended sprints (file-event churn, disk).

run: import sys; sys.exit(0 if 'def clean_runner_leftovers' in open('_tools/bl_land.py').read() else 1)

repro_reason: the defect is that the cleanup is a skill instruction run by an agent that may not run the commands; the match shows no python step does it
